title: When the Typewriter Sings
premise: In 1898, in a river town where ice governs the shipping season, Rosalind Marchetti works anonymously in the late Master Albrecht's map workshop, completing the atlas he died protecting from a syndicate that wants its trade routes erased. When a sealed letter surfaces naming Rosalind's family as complicit in the syndicate's plot, the town's suspicion falls on them, and Rosalind must prove their innocence by finishing the atlas and exposing the truth hidden in Albrecht's marginalia. As the river ice groans toward its spring break, Rosalind races to complete the final plates, outwit the syndicate's agent, and claim their name openly. The atlas is delivered, the family is cleared, and Rosalind signs the finished work with their own full name for the first time.
about_author: Petra Coldharbour is the pen name of a former cartographer's clerk who spent a decade cataloguing antique atlases in northern archives. Their novels are known for meticulous period detail and protagonists who speak with their hands.

chapters.title: The Quiet Hand
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Introduces the workshop, the unfinished atlas, and Rosalind's habit of working without credit. They ink coastlines by lamplight while the master's empty chair gathers dust. Emotional beat: grief channeled into diligence, and the comfort of anonymity.

chapters.title: What the Master Left
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Inventorying Albrecht's effects, Rosalind finds the atlas two plates short of complete and a locked drawer they were never permitted to open. The syndicate's agent, Herr Voss, arrives asking polite questions. Emotional beat: first unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: The Letter Under Wax
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The drawer yields a sealed letter addressed to the Marchetti family, naming them in a plot to falsify river charts for the syndicate. Rosalind reads it twice and burns neither the letter nor their composure. Emotional beat: the floor drops out of a careful life.

chapters.title: Names Are Dangerous Things
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind hides the letter and visits their mother, who goes pale at the family name spoken aloud. Hints of an old bargain made by Rosalind's late father surface. Emotional beat: inherited shame, unexplained.

chapters.title: Voss at the Door
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The syndicate's agent surveys the workshop, praising Rosalind's linework while measuring the room for leverage. He offers to buy the atlas unfinished. Rosalind refuses with a steady voice and shaking hands. Emotional beat: the predator's patience.

chapters.title: The Marginalia
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Studying Albrecht's pencil notes, Rosalind realizes the master suspected chart falsification and encoded evidence in the atlas's own plates. The work becomes a testimony. Emotional beat: the dead man speaking through ink.

chapters.title: Ice on the River
chapters.summary: Tomas, a wharf clerk and Rosalind's only friend, narrates. The ice is thick and late; the town bets on the break-up date. Voss books passage on the first barge. Emotional beat: a ticking clock made of frozen water.

chapters.title: An Accusation in Public
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A town councilman produces a copy of the letter; the Marchetti name is read aloud in the guild hall. Rosalind says nothing, which reads as guilt. Emotional beat: invisibility curdling into exposure.

chapters.title: Mother's Silence
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind confronts their mother, who finally admits the father took syndicate money once, to feed the family, and never touched a chart. The letter is blackmail, not proof. Emotional beat: anger giving way to understanding.

chapters.title: The Missing Plates
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Two atlas plates are gone from the workshop. Rosalind deduces Voss stole them to force a bargain: the atlas's silence for the family's cleared name. Emotional beat: cornered, but now certain of Voss's guilt.

chapters.title: A Bargain Rejected
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss offers Rosalind restoration of the family name in exchange for burning the atlas. Rosalind counters that the truth needs no trade. Voss leaves a threat wrapped in courtesy. Emotional beat: the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: Working by Candle-Ration
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The guild suspends the workshop's license pending inquiry. Rosalind works by night, redrawing the stolen plates from memory and Albrecht's field notes. Emotional beat: defiant craft as resistance.

chapters.title: Tomas Takes a Risk
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas finds one stolen plate hidden in a barge manifest and smuggles it to Rosalind, endangering his position. Their friendship deepens into trust. Emotional beat: loyalty chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: The Guild Inquiry
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind testifies, revealing the marginalia evidence but withholding the final plate's secret. The council wavers; Voss produces a forged confession bearing the father's name. Emotional beat: the noose tightening.

chapters.title: What the Father Knew
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Among the father's effects, Rosalind finds his own field journal proving he refused to falsify charts and reported Voss's predecessor. The letter's 'plot' was punishment for honesty. Emotional beat: grief transfigured into inheritance worth having.

chapters.title: The Last Plate
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind completes the final plate, embedding the syndicate's falsified route alongside the true one, so the atlas itself indicts them. Hands steady for the first time since the letter. Emotional beat: the work becoming a weapon.

chapters.title: The Ice Begins to Sing
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The river cracks and groans; the town gathers on the banks. Voss prepares to sail with the atlas if he can seize it. Rosalind sends the plates ahead by Tomas's barge. Emotional beat: the countdown made audible.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Workshop
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Voss comes for the atlas the night before the break-up. Rosalind stalls him, then reveals the finished plate and the father's journal. Voss moves to burn the workshop. Emotional beat: fear answered with a steady hand.

chapters.title: Fire on the Water
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The workshop catches; Rosalind saves the atlas at the cost of nearly everything else, escaping through the smoke as the ice breaks with a roar. Voss is caught by the harbor watch with the forged confession in his coat. Emotional beat: loss and deliverance in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Plates
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Before the guild and the town, the atlas's marginalia and the father's journal are read aloud. The Marchetti name is cleared; the syndicate's routes are struck from every copy. Emotional beat: vindication that feels quieter than hoped.

chapters.title: What Survives the Fire
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind surveys the charred workshop and decides to rebuild, taking apprentices as Albrecht once did. The mother and Rosalind reconcile over the father's true legacy. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed as choice.

chapters.title: Signed in Full
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The completed atlas is delivered on the first spring barge, and Rosalind signs the title plate with their full name—Marchetti and all. The river runs free. Emotional beat: identity no longer hidden, survival no longer silent.
